items.title: AI fails to compensate for night-shift fatigue among residents
items.excerpt: Evidence that AI can offset fatigue-related performance loss among night-shift radiology residents remains limited, a new study finds.

items.title: Biograph highlights cardiac AI CT study
items.excerpt: AI analysis of coronary CT angiography exams found elevated coronary inflammation in over 40% of asymptomatic, low-risk adults, Biograph reports.

items.title: Rivanna gets FDA clearance for BoneEnhance ultrasound software
items.excerpt: Rivanna received FDA clearance for BoneEnhance, a software module that identifies bone and surrounding tissues and highlights them with color-coded overlays on 2D B-mode ultrasound images.

items.title: Five AI tools for prostate cancer screening are recommended by NICE
items.excerpt: NICE has recommended five AI tools that highlight areas of possible prostate cancer on MRI for NHS use while further evidence on their accuracy is generated.

items.title: FDA Official Believes GenAI-enabled Tools Will Need to Be Assessed Like a Physician - MedCity News
items.excerpt: Rick Abramson, a radiologist by training and the director of FDA's Digital Health Center of Excellence said, "We ended up putting out this idea that maybe these devices are starting to behave a little bit more like me as a physician than a heart valve or a defibrillator."

items.title: Can AI diagnose like a team of doctors? New research puts it to the test
items.excerpt: Microsoft AI published new research testing whether its diagnostic orchestrator can work through complex cases like a panel of doctors, claiming it outperforms physicians on diagnostic accuracy.

items.title: Putting conversational AI to the test in primary care
items.excerpt: A patient-facing conversational AI showed promising feasibility and safety in a single-center primary care setting, providing a basis for larger-scale evaluation.

items.title: AI doctors’ orders come with a sky-high bill
items.excerpt: Large language models suggest more tests, referrals and medications than human physicians do, driving up the cost of care.
